sessions.phase_label: Untimestamped trailer specification, visual development, revision, and viability assessment

requirements.title: Conformity to the Revised Script
requirements.definition: Trailer content and shot directions must follow the revised script, with the script controlling where it explicitly differs from the older storyboard reel.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the authoritative content and shot-direction source for the artifact; communication logistics and the detailed content of individual scenes are excluded.

requirements.title: Text Card Production Responsibility
requirements.definition: Text cards are to be produced by the client rather than included in the freelancer's trailer-production work.
requirements.boundary_note: Retained as a distinct deliverable-boundary decision because it changes whether a future agent should create text-card assets.

requirements.title: Full-Color Final Video
requirements.definition: The final video must be rendered in full color rather than in the black-and-white treatment used for economical storyboard preparation.
requirements.boundary_note: Color treatment is independently enforceable and does not determine the video's orientation, medium, or animation quality.

requirements.title: Vertical 9:16 Video Format
requirements.definition: The video must use a vertical orientation with a 9:16 aspect ratio.
requirements.boundary_note: Aspect ratio and orientation form one tightly coupled output-format constraint.

requirements.title: Animation as the Primary Presentation Medium
requirements.definition: The project should first attempt an animated trailer rather than defaulting immediately to a still-frame presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers selection of animation as the primary medium; the conditional still-frame fallback and the required animation quality are separate decisions.

requirements.title: Digital Comic Fallback
requirements.definition: A digital comic composed of still frames may replace animation if animation produces poor results or proves too difficult or expensive.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a conditional alternative deliverable that can be activated independently of changes to the animated-trailer specifications.

requirements.title: Acceptable Animation Quality
requirements.definition: Animation must attain a quality level acceptable to the client before further contract resources are committed to full animation production.
requirements.boundary_note: Quality is an acceptance condition distinct from choosing animation as the primary medium; the evidence does not provide an objective numerical quality threshold.

requirements.title: Character Visual Style
requirements.definition: Character depictions must maintain the intended consistent style, ultimately favoring a raw graffiti aesthetic that is darker, rougher, less polished, and more sketch-like.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers stylistic treatment of the characters; preservation of identifying details and the one-off freelancer restyling task are independently actionable.

requirements.title: Character Detail and Feature Fidelity
requirements.definition: Generated character images must preserve the intended character details and recognizable features while applying the selected artistic style.
requirements.boundary_note: Character identity fidelity can succeed or fail separately from matching the broader graffiti-style treatment.

requirements.title: Three-Character Restyle Pass
requirements.definition: Apply the revised target style to Red Fern, Blue Lantern, and Kestrel and recreate the existing frames using the restyled characters.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the independently requested freelancer task whose responsibility can be withdrawn without removing the final artifact's character-style requirement.

requirements.title: Set Image Quality
requirements.definition: Set and background images must provide sufficient visual quality for the required shots, allowing new source images or adjusted shot angles when those improve the result.
requirements.boundary_note: New background generation and angle adjustment are means of satisfying image quality rather than separate Requirements; visual distinctness and stylistic continuity have separate acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Visual Distinctness Between Sets
requirements.definition: The revised sets must remain visibly distinct rather than becoming excessively similar to one another.
requirements.boundary_note: Set distinctness has its own observed failure trajectory and can be evaluated independently of resolution or overall rendering quality.

requirements.title: Set Style Continuity
requirements.definition: New or revised set images must remain stylistically on target and visually consistent across related shots.
requirements.boundary_note: Stylistic continuity across set images is separate from their technical quality and from the requirement that different sets remain distinguishable.

requirements.title: Character-Pair Framing Progression
requirements.definition: The three pairs of Kestrel and Red Fern images must progress from long or wide framing, to mid framing, to a closer waist-up framing.
requirements.boundary_note: Pair count, character inclusion, and wide-to-close order are attributes of one coordinated framing progression rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Opening Aerial Establishing Shot
requirements.definition: The opening sequence should include the intended aerial establishing shot, although it may be completed after higher-priority required material.
requirements.boundary_note: This shot has an independent defer/resume trajectory and is not the same as the wide framing required for the character-pair sequence.

requirements.title: Kestrel Background Bridge Composition
requirements.definition: Kestrel images must remove the bridge at his waist and the bridge above his head, leaving only the upper bridge so lower bridges do not interfere with the character.
requirements.boundary_note: The bridge arrangement is a specific independently verifiable composition correction, separate from cropping and character-shadow restoration.

requirements.title: Character Shadow Rendering
requirements.definition: Character shadows present in earlier renders must be retained or restored in revised character images without otherwise changing the approved composition.
requirements.boundary_note: Shadow presence has a concrete failure condition independent of character style, identity fidelity, and background bridge placement.

requirements.title: SQ4 Energy Blast
requirements.definition: SQ4 must include the energy-blast treatment described in the client's separately supplied notes.
requirements.boundary_note: The energy-blast work was independently authorized to continue while other work was paused; its detailed visual parameters are unavailable in the supplied messages.

requirements.title: SQ4 Shot Specifications
requirements.definition: The remaining SQ4 shots, including their required frame counts and framing, must follow the clarified client specifications for SQ4 rather than unsupported interpretation of the old storyboard.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the coordinated SQ4 shot and frame specification; the independently actionable energy-blast effect remains separate.

requirements.title: SQ11 Shot Specifications
requirements.definition: SQ11 must use the intended frames, frame count, and shot angles after reconciling the revised script with the outdated storyboard.
requirements.boundary_note: SQ11 is retained separately because its frames and angles can be clarified or modified without changing SQ12 or SQ4.

requirements.title: SQ12 Shot Specifications
requirements.definition: SQ12 must use the intended frames, frame count, and shot directions after reconciling the revised script with the storyboard.
requirements.boundary_note: SQ12 is independently evolvable from SQ11 even though one freelancer message raises uncertainty about both scenes.

unresolved_candidates.description: Several substantive review notes were sent outside the supplied message history by email, so any additional image-specific Requirements contained in those notes cannot be recovered safely.
The evidence raises possible changes to SQ5, SQ7, and SQ10 onward but contains no authoritative resolution or concrete changed values sufficient to define additional scene Requirements.
The target scene and acceptance criteria for the submitted footage and proposed 20-frame option are not sufficiently explicit to route them to one Requirement without additional context.

The client conditionally mentions further look refinement and animation tests, but it is unclear whether a standalone test artifact was commissioned or whether the message only describes evidence needed before proceeding.
The final project lifecycle is unresolved: the client expresses a desire to continue but conditions further work on confidence in achievable look and animation quality.
